key_insight: Use model uncertainty at test time to selectively and adaptively zoom into parts of a GUI screenshot so only genuinely ambiguous regions are reprocessed at higher resolution — improving localization of small/dense elements without retraining.
problem_solved: GUI grounding struggles with tiny icons and crowded layouts; existing test-time zoom-in methods apply fixed, uniform crops that waste compute and miss cases where zooming is or isn't needed.
method: Estimate per-query / per-region uncertainty from the base grounding model's outputs (confidence scores, probability gap or entropy) at the original scale — no additional training required.
Trigger adaptive, variable-size zoom crops only for regions/queries with high uncertainty and re-run inference on those crops (progressive or multi-scale as needed).
Fuse original-scale and zoomed predictions to produce final localizations, yielding better accuracy for small/dense elements while reducing unnecessary zooming and compute.
impact: Provides a plug-and-play, training-free way to improve GUI grounding accuracy and efficiency; practical for deploying stronger localization of small UI elements without retraining models or uniformly increasing inference cost.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: original screenshot -> uncertainty map -> selective zoom crops -> re-inference -> fused output

paper_title: UI-Zoomer: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Zoom-In for GUI Grounding
paper_authors: Fei Tang, Bofan Chen, Zhengxi Lu, Tongbo Chen, Songqin Nong
